paths.description: Landing/information template and first viewport; represents the public domain explanation.
Primary abuse-report journey, including empty validation and a valid submission.
Representative long legal/content template; terms and cookies pages share this template and were de-duplicated.
Recovery path for an unknown URL and HTTP-status handling.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light page, and the DOM reports color-scheme: normal with fixed light surface colors.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and adapt the surface, border, text, and control colors with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection finds no @view-transition rule or view-transition-name on the home and policy templates; footer navigation is a same-origin MPA route change.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an opt-in @view-transition navigation rule and restrained cross-document transition, while retaining reduced-motion behavior.

findings.summary: Long legal pages provide no position or section-navigation cue.
findings.evidence: The privacy template is about 2,916 CSS px tall and contains ten sections, but its DOM has only footer navigation and no sticky section navigation, progress indicator, or current-page cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a compact section table of contents or scroll-progress cue for long policy pages and indicate the current policy in the footer navigation.

findings.summary: The abuse-report flow depends on an external mail client and has no in-page completion state.
findings.evidence: A valid submission calls window.open() with a mailto: URL. There is no server submission, in-page success confirmation, saved state, or fallback contact address visible in the flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Submit to a protected server endpoint and show pending, success, and failure states; retain a clearly visible email fallback if mailto remains available.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return a misleading successful blank response.
findings.evidence: Fetching /definitely-not-found returns HTTP 200 text/plain “empty OK”; the screenshot offers no explanation, home link, retry, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an actual 404 status and a branded error document with a concise explanation, home link, and contact/retry options.

findings.summary: Contact fields have no persistent visible labels.
findings.evidence: All four controls rely on placeholder text; the DOM probe finds no associated label elements. The placeholder disappears during entry, removing the visible field identity even though Lighthouse’s automated accessibility score is 1.0.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit <label for> elements and keep placeholders only as optional examples or hints.

findings.summary: Pages lack descriptions and legal pages reuse a generic title.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no meta description. The privacy page H1 is “Privacy Policy” but its title is “Domain Information”, matching the homepage instead of uniquely describing the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each route a unique descriptive title and concise meta description aligned with its visible H1 and purpose.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent and unknown URLs are soft 404s.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse says robots.txt is invalid; /sitemap.xml returns plain text “empty OK”; no canonical is present; and an unknown route returns 200 instead of 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid robots.txt and XML sitemap, add appropriate canonical links, and return correct HTTP status codes for missing resources.

findings.summary: The public domain-information page has no share-preview or organization metadata.
findings.evidence: The document probe finds no Open Graph tags and no JSON-LD on the landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph metadata and minimal Organization/WebSite JSON-LD that matches the visible operator and domain-purpose content.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policy is weak despite HTTPS.
findings.evidence: The header probe finds no CSP, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. HSTS exists but max-age=1 provides effectively no durable downgrade protection.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP (including frame-ancestors), durable HSTS after rollout validation, and explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy headers.

findings.summary: The English document is identified correctly, but list layout uses physical-direction CSS.
findings.evidence: The DOM has lang="en", but authored CSS positions list markers with left: 0 and padding-left semantics, so it will not naturally mirror in RTL writing modes.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace physical left/right offsets and padding with inset-inline-start and padding-inline-start; set dir where localized content requires it.

findings.summary: The form explicitly disables useful autofill assistance.
findings.evidence: Every contact input and textarea has autocomplete="off", including name and email, forcing repeat visitors to retype standard identity fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Use appropriate autocomplete tokens such as name and email; omit autocomplete=off for subject and message unless there is a documented security reason.

taskList.title: Return correct 404 responses and add a useful recovery page
Deploy durable security and browser-policy headers
Replace the mailto-only report flow with an in-page submitted flow
Add visible form labels and useful autocomplete tokens
Repair titles, descriptions, canonical, robots, sitemap, and share metadata
Improve long-page navigation and route transitions
Use logical CSS properties for bidirectional layout
